subject: Provisioning lag impact and customer action plan
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sierralogix.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: SierraLogix Support <support@sierralogix.com>
Date: 2028-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: spike during load test — throttles and provisioning lag

Hi Vivek,

We just ran a scheduled load test against our Dedicated pool (region: us-west-2) and observed a sustained token-latency increase and intermittent 429s starting ~08:40 PDT. It looks like additional reserved nodes were not provisioned fast enough: our telemetry shows queue growth and request timeouts for ~22 minutes.

I've attached the condensed load capture (sierralogix-load-logs.txt) and pasted a short excerpt below: 

---
2028-10-19T08:41:12Z INFO request queued 4s
2028-10-19T08:43:05Z WARN token-latency 1200ms
2028-10-19T08:48:30Z ERROR 429 throttled
---

This is blocking our rollout tomorrow. Can you confirm root cause and ETA for mitigation? If necessary we'll throttle our testing, but we need a reliable remediation plan before we proceed with the next phase.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex Gomez
Director, MLOps | SierraLogix

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sierralogix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-19T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: spike during load test — immediate mitigations + next steps

Hi Alex — thank you for the logs and the quick heads-up. Sorry you're seeing this during a planned test. We're treating this as high priority.

Immediate things we're doing now (action items):
- Routing: temporarily enable routing to your warm-standby nodes to relieve the queuing pressure (will not change model).
- Concurrency: recommend limiting per-instance concurrency by 25% for the remainder of today's tests to keep tail latency under control.
- Fallback: if you approve, we can route a small percentage (10%) of traffic to a slightly smaller model variant we've validated with your prompts; this reduces latency while we remediate.
- Credits: we will propose a goodwill credit (TBD) if the window impacts your rollout.

I've looped Ben and Marissa to provide a technical diagnosis and a patch ETA; Laura will coordinate any changes to your Reserved Capacity contract if we need short-term additional capacity.

Can you confirm: are you okay with the 10% fallback routing and the temporary concurrency limit? If yes, we'll enact within 30 minutes.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Direct: +1-415-555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sierralogix.com>
Date: 2028-10-19T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: spike during load test — diagnostic and mitigation plan

Vivek / Alex — quick technical summary:
- Root cause: autoscaler headroom calculation under-estimated pending allocation because the scheduler's metadata write latency spiked when the control-plane DB GC kicked in; this meant the autoscaler thought nodes were already hot-adding when they were still pending.
- Observable: prolonged "provisioning" state (instances in pending for 18–24m) and queue amplification during that window.
- Short-term mitigation: we've implemented an interim heuristic to treat pending allocations as "not available" for headroom until they reach the 'healthy' heartbeat. This will stop the autoscaler from under-provisioning in similar bursts.
- Hotfix: a small change to the allocator (hotfix-diff.patch) which: (a) adds a heartbeat-backed headroom check, (b) adds a capped warm-standby incrementer, and (c) tightens retry windows for metadata writes. We will deploy to prod canary in us-west-2 tomorrow 03:00 UTC and ramp over 30 minutes.

Planned timeline:
- 2028-10-19 17:00 PDT: enable 10% fallback routing and apply concurrency limit (if Alex approves).
- 2028-10-20 03:00 UTC: deploy canary hotfix in us-west-2 (30 min ramp).
- 2028-10-20 05:00 UTC: monitor & rollback safety window; full rollout if green.

Risk & rollback: rollback path is immediate; canary is safe by design. We'll post the patch summary once the canary completes.

Ben Carter
Senior Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sierralogix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-19T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: spike during load test — mutual action plan and credits

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the 10% fallback. We've enacted the routing change and the concurrency cap at 10:20 PDT; your telemetry should show reduced queue growth within the next 10 minutes.

Mutual action plan (attached: mutual-action-plan.xlsx):
- Today (2028-10-19): routing + concurrency cap in place; SRE monitoring and daily status notes.
- 2028-10-20 03:00 UTC: canary deploy of hotfix to us-west-2; 30-minute ramp and monitoring.
- 2028-10-20 06:00 UTC: targeted full rollout if canary passes.
- Follow-up: detailed postmortem and proposed SLA credit within 72 hours after full rollout verification.

We are prepared to provision an extra Reserved node for 48 hours if you want guaranteed headroom during your rollout; Laura is standing by to confirm pricing/contract amendment. As a gesture of goodwill we will credit 10% of the affected period if the patch does not fully prevent recurrence.

Please confirm you received the routing change and whether you'd like us to provision the extra Reserved node for the 48-hour window.

Best,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
email: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sierralogix.com>

Date: 2028-10-20T16:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: spike during load test — provisioning lag impact and customer action plan

Vivek, Ben, Marissa — thanks for the clear plan and the quick action.

We saw the queue drop within 7 minutes after you enabled the routing change; that looks good. Please proceed with the canary tomorrow as scheduled.

We'd like you to provision the extra Reserved node for 48 hours starting 2028-10-20 20:00 UTC — please send the brief amendment and I'll route for approval. Also confirm the 10% goodwill credit path and the expected date for the postmortem.

One ask: can you include a daily status note tomorrow morning (UTC) and a short summary after the canary completes?

Thanks again,
Alex

Alex Gomez
Director, MLOps | SierraLogix
